name: JellyMesh
overview: Federates multiple Jellyfin servers into one library
description: JellyMesh shows films and series from other Jellyfin servers in your existing libraries and streams them through the local server. Duplicates become one title: a local copy always wins, otherwise the best quality does, and the other copies stay as backups. Remote servers can be stock Jellyfin or run JellyMesh, which adds shared libraries, stream limits and a change feed between servers you trust. An admin can merge films that can't be matched safely.

versions.changelog:
- After you choose to migrate automatically, JellyMesh now syncs the servers before it scans, so the migration no longer waits for the next scheduled sync with every old title waiting for a scan.
- A migration left waiting that way on 0.5.0.0 carries on by itself after the update, with no action.

Not verified: a remote server that is offline or fails during that sync, checked only in unit tests.

- JellyMesh now needs Jellyfin 12.1 or later: on 12.0, upgrade Jellyfin first.
- Each server now has its own Film and Serie folders inside the federated folder, so each server can have its own libraries and permissions.
- A title now shows once in each library, with the copies of every server and your local copy as versions: a local copy starts first, otherwise the best copy the user can see, and each user is offered only the versions they can see.
- "Watched" is now shared by all versions of a title, in every library, while the resume position stays with the version that was played.
- A local copy no longer removes the remote copies, so a library of server folders stays complete.
- When a version cannot play, playback now falls back only to the other versions the user can see, then to a local transcode, then to a local copy the user can see.
- A new switch on each server's card creates a Film and a Serie library for that server and keeps them in step with it; JellyMesh renames and deletes only the libraries it created, and user permissions stay with you.
- Servers can now be renamed from their card: their files and automatic libraries follow, the users allowed or blocked on those libraries are updated, and the watch state is carried.
- Adding a server that is already configured is refused, and the message names it.
- A server removed and added back is now treated as a new server, so link its folders to your libraries again unless automatic libraries do it.
- Removing a server now keeps each user's watch state for its titles for 90 days and puts it back when the same titles appear again, from that server or another one.
- Removing a server now stops what plays from it at once and ends its JellyMesh device on the remote, also after a restart, if the server answers within a few seconds; otherwise the device stays listed there.
- If the watch state of a removed server cannot be saved, its folders stay and the plugin page warns about it until the save succeeds.
- The kept watch state is saved in a file that only the user running Jellyfin can read.
- At the first start a banner asks whether to move from the old shared folders automatically or by hand; the old titles keep playing until the move is done, and the watch state moves to the new titles.
- A new setting adds the folders of servers connected later to your libraries automatically.
- Series can now be merged by hand too, episode by episode, and merged copies become versions instead of backups; favourite, rating and play count move to the primary version.
- Splitting or merging versions in Jellyfin itself is undone at the next sync: use Undo merge on the plugin page to separate copies.
- The plugin page now warns about a library over the whole federated folder or a server's folder, about libraries added to or removed from the federated folder, about series split across different libraries, and about a second library on a server's folders.
- Libraries that hold only federated folders are no longer offered to other JellyMesh servers, and federated titles are now left out at any depth of the federated folder, including through symbolic links, other Unicode forms of the path and macOS letter case.
- Seasons now come from the remote with their name, overview and poster, films and series also get their logo, banner and thumb, and images removed on the remote are deleted.
- YouTube trailers of remote titles now show in Jellyfin.
- Intro and credits segments now come from the remote, also from JellyMesh servers on 0.5, and are dropped when playback falls back to a copy of a different length.
- A new option, off by default, writes remote collections into films so that Jellyfin groups them; JellyMesh servers send their collections from 0.5.
- New local films and series without provider IDs now get one metadata refresh, so that they can be matched with remote copies.
- The Catalog tab now shows the last 50 syncs and the last 7 nightly reconciliations, with counts for each server.
- JellyMesh now writes to Jellyfin's activity log when a server goes offline or comes back, when a sync fails, when saved passwords no longer decrypt, and for each completed sync.
- If a source drops during playback, the retry now plays from another source, and a title that drops more than 3 times within 5 minutes is refused until they pass.
- A stream slot freed by revoking a library, lowering a limit or abandoning a stream now stays counted until its transcode is closed.
- Users who can't see a version or a title of a server can no longer reach it through the legacy segment, audio and playlist routes, and non-admins can no longer play a version that is in no library.
- Syncs that find nothing new finish faster; files changed by hand in the federated folder are put right by the nightly reconciliation.
- Going back to 0.4 after 0.5 has started is not supported: 0.4 discards the new state, and would read series merged by hand as films.

Not verified: playback and sync on Jellyfin 12.1, where only installing and loading were checked; how the Android TV and Swiftfin apps show versions, read only from their source; Next Up with two versions of an episode; the sync history in a real Jellyfin; trailers of series; Jellyfin creating the collections from remote collections; the federated folder recognized through links on macOS and Windows; a stream that breaks in the middle of its body, and the HLS reconnection; intro and credits segments read from a real remote; the kept watch state on Jellyfin 12.1 to 12.3, where only 12.4 was tried; the kept watch state of titles moved from the 0.4 layout, checked only in unit tests; a slow client may play a few more seconds from its buffer after a removed server's stream ends; the warning for a removal that cannot save the watch state, checked only with a simulated failure; the private watch state file on Windows, where SQLite's side files take the folder's permissions.

- A request for a video segment that names no play session can no longer stop another user's transcode on this server: it is refused only when it names the device of another user's play session, or when it names no device while another user has a transcode without one. Playlists are not affected.
- Servers that play titles you share through JellyMesh can no longer reach each other's play sessions, including through the legacy params or a query with different letter case.
- Servers you share with can no longer open live TV through a shared title: their stream and PlaybackInfo requests that name a live stream are refused.
- Users of this server can no longer stop, restart or keep alive a stream that another JellyMesh server plays from it.

Not verified: that the end of an idle stream slot, rather than Jellyfin itself, closes a quiet transcode of another server, with the setting on or off; a music client that sends no device.

- The plugin records which server last served each federated title to each user, ready for the per-server folders of 0.5.
- Another user can no longer stop, restart or keep alive a federated title you play through this server's own transcode by naming its play session, even during a long pause or after the title is renamed or removed.
- Start, progress and ping reports of another user on that play session are answered without effect.
- Another user can no longer stop that transcode with a request that names your device and no play session.
- Each user keeps at most 256 of these play sessions; beyond that the least recently used one leaves first.

Not verified: a long pause on a real client, and the record of the last server across a plugin upgrade.

- Stock streaming, subtitle, attachment and trickplay requests check the federated title they name, also as the version picked with mediaSourceId, videoId or the legacy params: without a signed-in user they get 401, and a user who cannot see the title gets 404.
- A stock stream can no longer reuse the play session of a federated title to reach it from another title.
- An anonymous attachment request no longer makes the server refresh a federated title.
- The page no longer warns about a library that holds the federated folder together with other folders: it counts as linked.
- The README explains that a user connected as a server cannot use that server from an app or the web client.

Not verified: a play session reused from another title is covered by unit tests only, not on a running server.

The credential key now lives in a file the plugin creates in its data folder, so JELLYMESH_SECRET_KEY is no longer needed: credentials saved with it move to the file once at startup. If saved passwords can no longer be read, the page asks for them again on each server. On Windows the key file gets an explicit access list (the account running Jellyfin, SYSTEM, Administrators); this is not yet tried on a Windows server. Only removing a server from the page deletes its content, so an emptied settings file no longer wipes the federated folder; the Catalog tab offers to forget servers missing from the settings. A server whose removal cannot be saved stays configured, and a removed server's copies leave the manual merges. Films that a remote groups into collections now reach the library, large catalogs materialize much faster, and sync reads retry brief remote errors. The .strm endpoint refuses requests that come through a proxy; the README covers the reverse proxy case.

Redesigns the plugin page around the JellyMesh identity, in a dark and a light scheme that follow the Jellyfin theme, and shows it in English or Italian according to the language set in Jellyfin. After connecting a server, the page goes straight to choosing its libraries. Removing a server now deletes its content right away, while titles also on another server stay and move to it. The first setup step says what to do about the secret key. Remote playback is checked only on 12.4, with jellyfin-web only: real Android and TV clients and QSV are not yet tested.

Adds a logo, shown in the plugin catalog, and a JellyMesh entry in the Plugins section of the Dashboard menu. The federated folder can now be set with the JELLYMESH_FEDERATED_ROOT environment variable, which then wins over the plugin page. The logo and the menu entry are checked on Jellyfin 12.0 and 12.4, and remote playback only on 12.4, with jellyfin-web only: real Android and TV clients and QSV are not yet tested.

Loads on every Jellyfin 12.x. Earlier versions were built against the 12.4 packages, so older 12.x servers installed them and then showed them as NotSupported. The plugin page is checked on Jellyfin 12.2 and 12.4, and remote playback only on 12.4, with jellyfin-web only: real Android and TV clients and QSV are not yet tested.

A redesigned plugin page, split into five tabs and built from Jellyfin's own controls. It adds a health summary, first-run steps and status cards for servers, says how each action ended and what a removal will do, and picks the federated folder in Jellyfin's folder browser. Doubtful films now show the quality of each copy and what a merge would play. Tested on Jellyfin 12.4 with jellyfin-web only: real Android and TV clients and QSV are not yet tested.

First release, for Jellyfin 12.x. Films and series from stock and JellyMesh remotes, with dedup and per-episode completion, written to a federated folder you link to your libraries. Remote playback through the local server, with backup sources and a local transcode as fallback. Shared libraries and stream limits between JellyMesh servers, and manual film merges. Tested on Jellyfin 12.4 with jellyfin-web only: real Android and TV clients and QSV are not yet tested.
